title: Two letters, one sound
goal: Read sh as one sound and blend it with other taught correspondences.
evidence: Student blends shop without separating s and h, then reads Sam is in a shop.; check a different sh word.
lesson: After teaching sh; use ship as the next independent word.
brief: Heading 'Two letters can make one sound'. THREE connected sound circles, first contains sh together, next o, next p. Sentence strip 'Sam is in a shop.' Badge 'Teacher set: s a t p i n m d g o sh'. Keep sound circles B paper textures, mascot, colours, logo. 'Record my reading', 'Sound help', footer 'Word → Sentence → New word'. No shop illustration that reveals word, no separate circles for s and h, no prerecorded waveform or completed score.
prompt: Edit the provided app screenshot. Change ONLY the sentence 'Sam is in a shop.' to 'Sam sat in a shop.' Keep sh o p circles and everything else exactly. This avoids an untaught /z/ pronunciation of s. Maintain 4:3.
